title: Derived Hom from a finite locally free sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme and let $P$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module, meaning it is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus d}$ on an open cover for finite ranks $d$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Let $L$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-module viewed in degree zero [def-pc-derived-category]. Then the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is represented by the sheaf $\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] in degree zero; equivalently, the sheaves $\mathcal E xt^i_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,L)$ vanish for every $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (R Hom(K,M) = M tensor^L K^vee for K perfect; a finite locally free module is perfect)

proof.text: The dual of P is finite locally free (Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.dual, via the existing local free Hom calculation). Evaluation [lem-sc-ext-evaluation] gives a natural isomorphism tensorLeft(P dual) ≅ Hom(P,-). TensorLeft(P dual) preserves finite limits and colimits by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. Transport both preservation properties through the natural isomorphism; call the exact additive sheaf Hom functor T.

Choose the functorial K-injective resolution eta:L[0]→I(L[0]). Its map is a quasi-isomorphism and its target K-injective. The representative comparison [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies derived Hom(P[0],L[0]) with Q Hom-complex(P[0],I(L[0])). The new complex comparison [lem-sc-hom-complex-single] identifies this with Q(T applied degreewise to I(L[0])).

Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology applies to the exact additive T: T(eta) is a quasi-isomorphism. Invert its image under Q. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex then identifies degreewise T(L[0]) with Hom(P,L)[0]. Compose these isomorphisms to prove the first clause.

A derived single object at zero is IsLE zero by Mathlib DerivedCategory.TStructure. DerivedCategory.isZero_of_isLE gives zero homology in every strictly positive degree. Transport this IsZero property through the homology functor applied to the isomorphism just constructed.
